PullRequest.Title: Model router: add a command to open the routers folder
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #349131

A model router file that the model picker does not list could not be found from VS Code. The only way to a router file was the link in a listed router's Details, so a file whose rename dropped the `.model-router.yaml` ending left nothing to follow.

This adds **Chat: Open Model Routers Folder** to the Command Palette. It shows `~/.agents/model-routers` in the file manager, as **Open Logs Folder** and **Open Extensions Folder** do for their folders.

- The folder is created first when it does not exist yet, so the command also works before the first router is written.
- The command is offered on desktop while `chat.copilot.modelRouter.enabled` is on, in the editor window and in the Agents window.
- It is not offered in a remote window. The routers of a remote agent host are on its machine, where there is no local folder to show.
- Routers are also read from `~/.copilot/model-routers`. The command opens only `~/.agents/model-routers`, the folder routers are written to.

The host and the command now share one helper for the folder's path.

### How to test

1. Turn on `chat.copilot.modelRouter.enabled`.
2. Run **Chat: Open Model Routers Folder** from the Command Palette. The file manager opens `~/.agents/model-routers`, with a router file selected when the folder has one.
3. Delete the folder and run the command again. The folder is created and shown.
4. Turn the setting off. The command is no longer in the Command Palette.

### Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the 6 changed files: passed
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/{platform/agentHost/test/**/*odelRouter*,workbench/contrib/chat/test/electron-browser/actions/openModelRoutersFolderAction}.test.js"`: 76 passing. This ran with the change applied to an earlier commit of `main`; one import line in `copilotAgent.ts` was merged by hand there.
- Steps 1, 2 and 4 above in the Agents window on macOS, in a build from that same commit: passed. Step 3 is covered by the unit test.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The awaited action, unconditional metadata resolution in FileService.createFolder, per-child stat branch in toFileStat, and desktop provider's channel.call('stat') are all traced. These requests are concurrent, not N serialized round trips. Directory sizes and actual filesystem latency are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: N child-stat IPC requests and filesystem metadata operations, plus an extra directory listing and discarded file-stat objects.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: N is all immediate directory entries, not just valid or deduplicated routers. For an existing folder, each invocation makes N child-stat requests plus three folder-stat requests and two readdir requests; child stats run concurrently but the action awaits the entire batch. No application cache removes this work.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Avoidable folder-reveal latency and filesystem/IPC traffic on every invocation, including warm invocations.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The base had no model-router folder command and therefore no creation/metadata pass on this reveal path. Its existing folder-reveal pattern, such as OpenExtensionsFolderAction, used one non-metadata resolve followed by showItemInFolder. The newly required missing-folder creation does not require a metadata pass over an already existing folder.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Opening an existing routers folder now performs a metadata-resolving creation pass, followed by a second directory listing, before revealing one child. For N immediate entries this adds N independent child-stat IPC/filesystem requests that the action does not consume.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added unconditional await fileService.createFolder(folder) at line 46 invokes FileService.createFolder's resolve(resource, { resolveMetadata: true }) even when mkdirp finds the directory already exists. FileService.toFileStat then calls provider.stat for every immediate child. The added line 47 separately resolves the same folder without metadata.
Findings.Title: Avoid metadata-resolving creation for an existing routers folder
Findings.Impact: Users opening an existing folder containing saved router variants or renamed/backup files wait for metadata retrieval for every immediate entry before the file manager appears. This produces avoidable filesystem/IPC traffic and increasing reveal latency as the folder grows, especially with a slow home-directory filesystem.
Findings.Evidence: FileService.createFolder (src/vs/platform/files/common/fileService.ts:1007-1015) always resolves with resolveMetadata:true after mkdirp. toFileStat (:271-277) lists the folder and maps every entry to provider.stat(childResource), awaiting all results. The desktop DiskFileSystemProvider delegates to DiskFileSystemProviderClient, whose stat (:81-82) issues one main-process IPC call per entry. The action discards this result and performs another resolve at line 47; showItemInFolder at line 49 cannot start until both passes finish.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve the folder without metadata first. Only call createFolder when that resolve fails with FILE_NOT_FOUND, and use its returned children on that cold path. This preserves first-use creation and file selection while avoiding the per-entry metadata pass and second listing for existing folders.

Scenarios.Scenario: Desktop editor and Agents-window startup and Command Palette registration, including disabled and remote contexts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each desktop entry point imports the action and registerAction2 constructs its command metadata synchronously. The constructor does not invoke run or access filesystem/native services. Context conditions control palette visibility without opening or scanning the folder.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One additional action registration per window; fixed-size context expression and command metadata. The editor and Agents window have separate contribution entry points.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous constant-size registration. Filesystem and native operations remain deferred until explicit command invocation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Normal module reuse applies; modelRouter already has runtime consumers in the shared agent-host chat subsystem. No new folder cache, negative cache, or eager directory read is initialized by registration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: registerAction2 only constructs the action and installs its handler/menu entries; all new expensive operations reside in run.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Incremental module-loading and registration duration is unmeasured; no heavyweight initialization or collection-dependent startup operation was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable startup regression, hidden eager scan, or new long-lived resource ownership.

Scenarios.Scenario: Explicitly open an already existing local model-routers directory, populated or empty
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action awaits createFolder, then a second resolve, then native showItemInFolder. The first await includes a metadata stat for every immediate entry, so revealing the folder waits for the complete child-stat batch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Renderer-to-main filesystem stat and readdir requests through the desktop disk provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: With N immediate entries, an existing directory causes three folder-stat requests, two readdir requests, and N child-stat requests per invocation: N+5 filesystem IPC calls. N includes invalid, renamed, duplicate-name, and backup entries; model-catalog grouping does not apply.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No model-router folder command existed. Existing folder-reveal actions used a single non-metadata resolve, not an unconditional creation pass that resolves child metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All creation/metadata requests finish before the second listing, and both finish before the native reveal call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Directory enumeration and SymlinkSupport.stat for folder and child metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three folder metadata operations, two directory enumerations, and N explicit child metadata operations. Each enumeration also resolves symbolic-link targets for S immediate symlinks; there are two such enumerations. Symlink metadata can involve more than one underlying filesystem syscall.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The new unconditional createFolder adds one listing and N child metadata operations beyond the ordinary non-metadata resolve/reveal pattern. The underlying provider implementation is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The action waits for these filesystem operations through their IPC responses.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: One nativeHost proxy request invoking Electron shell.showItemInFolder with the first child's path, or the folder path when empty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per command invocation, not one per entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No dedicated model-router folder action; the native reveal service already existed and other reveal commands used the same single native call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Issued only after both filesystem passes finish; initiates the user-visible file-manager reveal.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All N immediate directory entries, plausibly saved router variants and renamed or backup files. Empty directories have N=0; subdirectories are not recursively scanned by either default resolve.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Top-level stages are sequential. Child metadata requests are issued concurrently via the entry map/Promises.settled, with no action-level global limiter; each invocation awaits all of them. Overlapping command invocations are not coalesced. This is N concurrent requests, not N sequential round trips.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application-level filesystem result cache or in-flight coalescing exists on this path. Existing-folder invocations repeat the metadata pass even when the directory is already known to exist. OS caching may reduce I/O duration but does not remove IPC or allocation. preferLocal userHome returns the stored local URI synchronously.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed unconditional createFolder call, its mandatory resolveMetadata:true pass, per-entry provider.stat branch, desktop IPC implementation, and ordering before native reveal are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Directory-size prevalence and elapsed latency are unmeasured. Small or empty folders incur only modest overhead; more entries or slow home-directory storage increase the effect. This limits severity to low, not confidence in the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one low-severity boundary-fanout finding at the added line 46. Extra enumeration and allocation share that root cause and are not separate findings.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Find the nearest existing ancestor and create missing directories, resolve the newly created empty folder, perform the action's second resolve, then reveal it. Existing router-catalog watchers may react to folder creation independently; their subsequent scan is not awaited by this action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat ancestor paths, mkdir missing directories, and resolve/list the new folder via the desktop filesystem channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For M missing directory components and a stable empty result, M+1 ancestor/folder checks, M mkdir requests, two additional folder stats and two listings: 2M+5 filesystem IPC requests. Under an existing user home, normally M is one or two. No child-stat fanout occurs for an empty folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The dedicated command and its first-use creation did not exist. Creation is intentionally required so the new command can reveal a previously absent folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Creation and both resolves are awaited before native reveal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Underlying filesystem metadata checks, nonrecursive mkdir for each missing component, and directory enumeration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Scales with missing path depth, normally one or two directories below the user home; two listings of the new empty folder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No filesystem creation on this absent command path. Node disk-provider operations themselves are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited through the filesystem channel; bounded setup work required by first use.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reveal the empty folder in its parent through shell.showItemInFolder.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No dedicated first-use reveal command; the native service already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initiates the file-manager display once required directory creation completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Missing ancestor depth M, rather than router count. A concurrently populated directory can also reach the already-reported per-entry metadata mechanism.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Ancestor stat checks and mkdir operations are sequential by path order. Independent invocations can overlap, but this is a user-issued command rather than an automatic collection-wide burst. Existing catalog file-change handling schedules rescans with a 200ms RunOnceScheduler off the command's critical path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no negative-cache or coalesced first-use promise. Once created, later runs follow the existing-folder scenario. mkdirp tolerates FileExists races; no new retained cache state is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the bounded creation sequence and absence of child metadata requests in the empty case; unchanged watcher reactions do not gate reveal.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem and file-manager duration depend on the local environment. Normal missing-path depth is small and no large cold-start fanout is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Required first-use creation is not independently reportable. Avoiding the second listing is covered by the same bounded recommendation as the existing-folder finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent-host router discovery, rescans, and router-check tool folder selection after extracting userModelRouterFolder
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When enabled, the existing catalog scans the two priority folders and reads candidate router files. Consumers that call whenSettled await the latest scan. The helper computes exactly the previous joinPath expression; it introduces no work beyond that URI calculation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve two router directories and read each suffix-matching router file with the existing 32KiB size limit; checking a requested router also uses the existing readFile host callback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two directory resolves per scan, then one readFile operation per eligible candidate file across the two folders. Name precedence deduplication occurs after reading/parsing, so candidate reads are not reduced to the final unique-name count. Explicit checking additionally reads the selected file as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical directory priority, reads, size limits, and scan placement. The changed line substitutes userModelRouterFolder for the same resourceJoinPath(userHome, '.agents', MODEL_ROUTER_FOLDER) expression.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Catalog scans can gate whenSettled consumers; scans triggered solely by first folder creation are not awaited by the new reveal command.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check folder/ancestor existence and install nonrecursive watchers; move watchers when pending router directories are created.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two configured folders, with nearest-parent checks bounded by ancestry to userHome and watcher targets deduplicated when equal. Same watcher ownership and replacement logic as the base.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same paths, watch targets, ancestry walk, and MutableDisposable replacement applied before extracting the helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Watcher setup is started without awaiting it in the source constructor and does not add a new reveal prerequisite.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Candidate router files across two priority folders and ancestry checks for absent folders. Per-file size is already capped; router count has no new cap or new increase introduced by this PR.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Catalog sources, priority folders, and candidate file reads are serial in the existing loops. Repeated file-change events are debounced; generation checks control publication. Those policies are unchanged by the URI helper extraction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing catalog snapshots, generation checks, last parsed names, and 200ms rescan scheduler are unchanged. Cold scanning and warm snapshot consumption retain their original behavior; no new invalidation or retention policy is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the removed expression and helper body perform the same joinPath on the same home and suffix, and all catalog/tool I/O call sites remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Router counts and scan duration are unmeasured, but neither their multiplicity nor scheduling changes in the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression or concrete regression fix in the helper refactor. Existing scanning or cache opportunities are out of scope.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all six changed files and every diff page against base 742a9ae378720f2526ed7128fbc47ec2a285f1b1. Submitted one low-severity, high-confidence finding for unconditional createFolder causing per-entry metadata IPC before an existing directory is revealed. Checked startup registration, local command cold/warm behavior, native and filesystem boundaries, effective child concurrency, and unchanged agent-host catalog/helper behavior. Static read-only review; latency magnitudes are not measured. No qualifying regression-fix learning signal.
